references.text: Nehemiah describes how the people of Israel in the wilderness wanted to appoint a leader over themselves to return to Egypt, a direct reference to the rebellion in Numbers 14:4.
The people complained and expressed a wish to have died in Egypt, the same longing to return to Egypt as in Numbers 14:4.
The people complained against Moses and asked why he had brought them out of Egypt, expressing the same dissatisfaction and desire to return.
The people remembered the food in Egypt and longed to go back, showing the same attitude of wanting to return to Egypt.
The verse just before, where the people explicitly say it would have been better to return to Egypt.
Moses warns against turning the people back to Egypt, a reminder of the forbidden longing to return.
In his speech, Stephen describes how the fathers refused to obey Moses but rejected him and in their hearts turned back to Egypt.
